title: Left-handed drummers
summary: Francis is left-handed with a left-foot bass drum beat; others noted include Alfred Williams, Red Duguay, Snags Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: You see, you're a left-handed drummer, aren't you? Yeah. Were there any other left-handed drummers in the old days that you can remember? I couldn't have. When you were a kid that you saw? I can't understand.
See, that's why I was kind of back with the jazz, because when I took left, I had a beat with my right foot, you see. When I went down the jazz, I got a beat with my left foot, you see.
I never noticed, you used your left foot, put that on the bass drum. Left-handed, yeah.
That's easier for you, is it?
I start that way, you see, yeah. But it's all the same.
See, there's Alfred Williams, that's left-handed. Yeah. Alfred left-handed? Yeah.
I didn't notice. I know Alfred well. I forgot to call his name. Yeah, Alfred Williams. I had a fella too, he told you about Red Duguay?
Remember him? Yeah, he was drunk, Red Duguay. Was he left-handed?

No, he wasn't left-handed. I knew one other drummer in Chicago was left-handed, Snaggs. Clifford Jones was his name. He came from here, but he went up there when he was pretty young. They called him Snaggs. He played with Joe Oliver and some of the people there. Did you ever play with Joe Oliver?
